# REQ-029 peer mesh sources and qualification gates

Reviewed 2026-11-23 against publisher documentation, release notes, and selected source. The retired roadmap and its earlier T069 entry preserve the project names and research remit. They do not preserve the full original comparison or the quoted rankings. The findings cover the claim categories supplied for this review. Each positive finding describes documented or implemented behavior at the cited revision. Installed behavior, radio performance, interoperability, adoption, and the frequency of the Mesh Talk problem remain unmeasured. [Retired roadmap](https://github.com/OctopusGarage/mesh-talk/blob/6b28c838%5E/docs/development-roadmap.md) · [Original T069 entry](https://github.com/OctopusGarage/mesh-talk/blob/e5133000/docs/development-roadmap.md)

## Columba

- **Calls and media.** The native Android app implements private live audio calls using LXST. The code maps call profiles to Codec2 and Opus, and a beta release documents mid-call quality and half/full-duplex negotiation. LXMF separately carries recorded voice messages, photos, and file attachments. The attachment and voice changes are evidence of sending actual media bytes. NomadNet page browsing and Markdown/link rendering are separate capabilities. Generic file transfer may carry a video file if it meets the relevant limits. The reviewed evidence establishes neither native video calling nor dedicated video streaming/playback. [Pinned app README](https://github.com/torlando-tech/columba/blob/f051982a416b1c96a687f56c69c8d164628f4f9c/README.md) · [Call profiles](https://github.com/torlando-tech/columba/blob/f051982a416b1c96a687f56c69c8d164628f4f9c/app/src/main/java/network/columba/app/ui/model/CodecProfile.kt) · [Call negotiation release](https://github.com/torlando-tech/columba/releases/tag/v2.3.1-beta) · [Voice messages](https://github.com/torlando-tech/columba/pull/1075) · [File attachments](https://github.com/torlando-tech/columba/pull/185) · [Image handling](https://github.com/torlando-tech/columba/pull/254) · [Markdown rendering](https://github.com/torlando-tech/columba/pull/1064)
- **Transport and hardware.** Peer BLE uses a compatible device's Bluetooth hardware and can work outside an IP LAN. The upstream BLE interface README is for Linux with BlueZ. Columba uses its own native Android implementation of that interface. Local Wi-Fi uses a reachable network. TCP needs a reachable Reticulum endpoint, which can be local or remote. LoRa requires compatible external RNode hardware and a configured radio path. Bluetooth or USB can connect the phone to the RNode, with LoRa used between radios. The project's LoRa-to-fiber call claim is a statement about available profiles. A viable call depends on the end-to-end route, airtime, duplex mode and loss. The site range figures are first-party estimates with no qualifying measurements in this review. [Columba site](https://columba.network/) · [BLE implementation](https://github.com/torlando-tech/ble-reticulum/blob/63557acfe5c923dcdafeb7bc37508bf835f16514/README.md) · [RNode release changes](https://github.com/torlando-tech/columba/releases/tag/v2.4.3-beta) · [Radio hardware manual](https://reticulum.network/manual/hardware.html#rnode)
- **Identity, routing and release scope.** Columba makes local cryptographic identities that can be shared by QR and exported or imported. Messages use LXMF over Reticulum. It can participate in forwarding, and LXMF propagation provides a separate offline delivery option when available. The v2.4.5-beta notes distinguish the recommended Python/reference backend from the experimental Kotlin stack and list APK variants, including builds without Sentry. The site says Android 12 or newer while the reviewed Gradle source sets \`minSdk = 24\`. Treat Android 12+ as the advertised requirement and the actual install and support floor as unverified for each signed artifact. [Columba site](https://columba.network/) · [Pinned app README](https://github.com/torlando-tech/columba/blob/f051982a416b1c96a687f56c69c8d164628f4f9c/README.md#what-you-can-do) · [APK releases](https://github.com/torlando-tech/columba/releases/tag/v2.4.5-beta) · [Gradle config](https://github.com/torlando-tech/columba/blob/f051982a416b1c96a687f56c69c8d164628f4f9c/app/build.gradle.kts#L161)

## Reticulum, LXMF and LXST

- **Reticulum** supplies addressing, link establishment and forwarding over configured interfaces. The local AutoInterface uses link-local IPv6 and UDP over an Ethernet or Wi-Fi medium, including a direct Ethernet cable. It can operate without a router, DHCP, or WAN, provided the local link exists. Other interfaces can use TCP/UDP over IP, or compatible hardware such as serial, KISS packet radio and RNodes using raw LoRa. The RNode radio link uses LoRa modulation. LoRaWAN is a different protocol. [Interfaces](https://reticulum.network/manual/interfaces.html) · [Hardware](https://reticulum.network/manual/hardware.html) · [Reticulum reference implementation](https://github.com/markqvist/Reticulum)
- **Addresses and routing.** Signed destination announcements provide public-key and path information. Configured Transport Nodes learn next hops and can forward between compatible interfaces. Endpoint instances have transport disabled by default. The manual distinguishes destination-addressed encrypted packets, authenticated encrypted links, pre-shared-key group destinations, and plaintext destinations. Forward secrecy depends on destination type and mode. These identities and destination proofs do not establish Mesh Talk account ownership, linked-device membership, or authorization. [Reticulum transport, announces and link design](https://reticulum.network/manual/understanding.html#the-reticulum-transport-system) · [Network topologies](https://reticulum.network/manual/networks.html)
- **LXMF** defines the signed message format and delivery layer over Reticulum, including file, image and audio fields. The router handles path lookup, delivery confirmation and retries. LXMF Propagation Nodes can hold and synchronize encrypted messages for later pickup when a recipient is unavailable. Routing and propagation therefore solve different parts of delivery. Forward-secrecy claims must be scoped to the delivery mode. An exported LXMF URI or QR can carry a serialized encrypted message itself. Ordinary URLs in chat reference separate content that still needs a reachable origin or cached copy. [LXMF format, router, propagation and encryption](https://github.com/markqvist/LXMF/blob/7dfc8353541f46e1c5aceab4849136dc28bb7855/README.md) · [LXMF field constants](https://github.com/markqvist/LXMF/blob/7dfc8353541f46e1c5aceab4849136dc28bb7855/LXMF/LXMF.py#L12)
- **LXST** is the separate real-time signal/streaming protocol. Its upstream describes live telephony, voice/audio codecs, and encrypted streams using Reticulum. Codec bitrate and upstream latency figures do not establish call quality through a given RF route. The author states that development moved to Reticulum-hosted source and that updates also ship on PyPI. If evaluating reuse, pin the actual distributed source, dependencies and backend, check license obligations and maintenance provenance, and test the chosen peer pair and transport. [LXST upstream README](https://github.com/markqvist/LXST/blob/6a329bf6d956ca8b15077d4c470afe4cb7c669cc/README.md) · [Reticulum ecosystem manual](https://reticulum.network/manual/software.html)

## Bitchat

- **Transport and routing.** The Permissionless Tech Apple and Android projects use nearby BLE with no infrastructure LAN or internet. Reach depends on compatible radios, permissions and nearby participating devices. The Apple whitepaper describes bounded relaying with TTL and deduplication, using known source routes where possible and controlled flooding on fallback. Sender retry and bounded text couriers can improve delivery across temporary partitions. Internet-based Nostr relays carry public geohash rooms and private fallback for mutual favorites. Android also documents Wi-Fi Aware on supported hardware and an Android foreground service subject to OS limits. Neither platform's docs establish reliable relay operation during lock, sleep, or background execution on every device. [Pinned Apple whitepaper §§2–6](https://github.com/permissionlesstech/bitchat/blob/04995f68e470a18d1fc99f86fa326c2a87bab4f2/WHITEPAPER.md) · [Android README](https://github.com/permissionlesstech/bitchat-android/blob/cc1fb178e2f33841cf026efbfbae27457f1c7763/README.md)
- **Encryption and identity.** The whitepaper documents Noise XX and forward secrecy for live private mesh sessions, Noise X for offline courier seals, and Bitchat-specific encrypted Nostr envelopes for private fallback. It documents the lack of forward secrecy for the latter two paths. Public mesh posts are signed broadcasts. The documented on-air peer ID is derived from a locally generated stable Noise key, and announcements expose linkable public identity data. QR/fingerprint verification is a distinct trust step. Android documents optional password protection for topic channels. Apply that claim at the Android feature boundary pending corroboration for the other clients. [Pinned Apple whitepaper §§3, 5, 7–9](https://github.com/permissionlesstech/bitchat/blob/04995f68e470a18d1fc99f86fa326c2a87bab4f2/WHITEPAPER.md#3-identity) · [Android channel documentation](https://github.com/permissionlesstech/bitchat-android/blob/cc1fb178e2f33841cf026efbfbae27457f1c7763/README.md#features) · [Android QR verification release](https://github.com/permissionlesstech/bitchat-android/releases/tag/1.6.0)
- **Media.** Apple documents real files/images fragmented over the mesh, a 1 MiB payload cap, receive acceptance, and text-only couriers. Private DM photos and voice notes are encrypted before BLE fragmentation as documented in the Apple v1.7.1 release. Accepted media stored by the Apple app relies on platform data protection. Apple v1.8.0 and Android v2.2.0 contain live push-to-talk audio for public mesh or DMs in addition to recorded voice notes. This is burst audio. The reviewed artifacts establish no conventional dial-and-answer full-duplex calling, live video, generic large-file parity, or media delivery by text couriers. Full cross-platform behavior for voice bursts and files needs a device test. [Apple payload limit](https://github.com/permissionlesstech/bitchat/blob/v1.8.0/localPackages/BitFoundation/Sources/BitFoundation/FileTransferLimits.swift#L4) · [Apple private media release](https://github.com/permissionlesstech/bitchat/releases/tag/v1.7.1) · [Apple live voice protocol](https://github.com/permissionlesstech/bitchat/blob/v1.8.0/bitchat/Protocols/VoiceBurstPacket.swift#L21) · [Android live voice implementation](https://github.com/permissionlesstech/bitchat-android/blob/v2.2.0/app/src/main/java/com/bitchat/android/features/voice/LiveVoiceManager.kt#L27) · [Android v2.2.0 release](https://github.com/permissionlesstech/bitchat-android/releases/tag/v2.2.0)

## Technitium Mesh

- **Confirmed publisher and requirements.** Mesh.im links to TechnitiumSoftware/Mesh. It succeeds the same publisher's Bit Chat client, which is a separate product line from Permissionless Tech Bitchat. The site labels Mesh alpha and lists Windows setup and portable packages. Its FAQ and source specify .NET Framework 4.6.1. Setup, portable launch, update, and current Windows compatibility remain unverified. [Project site](https://mesh.im/) · [FAQ](https://mesh.im/faq.html#q16) · [Official source](https://github.com/TechnitiumSoftware/Mesh) · [Windows target](https://github.com/TechnitiumSoftware/Mesh/blob/4a7dc4f4dab999143baa4247606089479805d61a/MeshApp/MeshApp.csproj#L13) · [Predecessor](https://github.com/TechnitiumSoftware/BitChatClient)
- **Transport, encryption, identity, and media.** The pure P2P profile uses reachable IP, including a private LAN with the WAN disconnected. DHT provides peer discovery, with separate local and internet paths in source and TCP relay code also present. The anonymous profile uses Tor and needs reachability to the Tor network. No BLE or LoRa path was established. The publisher documents an encrypted local RSA-2048 profile, a regenerable user ID verified out-of-band, ephemeral DH/ECDH key exchange, and authenticated AES-256 peer channels. Direct peers can see each other's IPs. No centralized registration is a narrower claim than absence of observable network metadata. Private and group chat support actual file attachments. The FAQ's suggestion to call a contact describes out-of-band verification. The reviewed first-party material establishes no built-in voice or video call. [FAQ §§1–4, 10–15](https://mesh.im/faq.html) · [Local DHT](https://github.com/TechnitiumSoftware/Mesh/blob/4a7dc4f4dab999143baa4247606089479805d61a/MeshCore/Network/DHT/DhtManager.cs#L234) · [TCP relay source](https://github.com/TechnitiumSoftware/Mesh/blob/4a7dc4f4dab999143baa4247606089479805d61a/MeshCore/Network/Connections/ConnectionManager.cs#L949) · [Attachment source](https://github.com/TechnitiumSoftware/Mesh/blob/4a7dc4f4dab999143baa4247606089479805d61a/MeshCore/Network/MeshNetwork.cs#L1441)

## Possible HostTalk match

- **tromoSM/HostTalk** is a strong name-and-purpose match. Its first-party README and v0.9 release describe a self-hosted local web chat with an invite URL and browser/PWA clients. The desktop host must be running and reachable on TCP port 6767. The main-branch implementation serves plain HTTP and uses Flask-SocketIO to broadcast messages and replay the last ten entries from host memory. Clients supply display names. The reviewed stock path provides no authenticated user identity or end-to-end encryption. A reachable LAN can suffice without internet. An unavailable host or absent IP path prevents this flow. The invite URL opens the chat UI. Calls, media transfer, and peer routing are unsupported by the examined evidence. The README claims multiple host platforms, while installability and mobile PWA behavior are still unknown. [Pinned README](https://github.com/tromoSM/HostTalk/blob/2e9ed3de46eec92d20fe40ac8894c82b8c1f3f92/README.md) · [v0.9 publisher release](https://github.com/tromoSM/HostTalk/releases/tag/v0.9) · [Host message path](https://github.com/tromoSM/HostTalk/blob/2e9ed3de46eec92d20fe40ac8894c82b8c1f3f92/server.py#L123) · [Host listener](https://github.com/tromoSM/HostTalk/blob/2e9ed3de46eec92d20fe40ac8894c82b8c1f3f92/server.py#L192)
- **Provenance gate.** Cite this repository as a candidate until the original author, URL, screenshot or equivalent identifier is recovered. The similarly named Fujitsu HostTalk integrates with VME mainframe applications. It supplies no evidence for the LAN messenger. [Fujitsu HostTalk datasheet](https://www.fujitsu.com/uk/imagesgig5/hosttalk-datasheet-uk.pdf)

## Candidate requirements and gates for Mesh Talk

The working scenario is a small team exchanging updates and a document on an existing LAN during an internet outage. Use current Mesh Talk messaging, member invitations, file offers and verified saved bytes as the baseline. Mesh Talk already has opt-in experimental direct voice and video. It requires a live Noise signaling route and separate reachable WebRTC candidates. The committed guide records synthetic browser media evidence across a routed VPN, with native macOS WebView and physical camera/mic quality still open. Historical REQ-023 covers voluntary group voice as a separate decision. [Mesh Talk calls](../docs/help/topics/calls.md) · [File and call topology scenarios](../docs/network-design-reference.md#s9--cross-site-call-request) · [Send files](../docs/help/topics/send-files.md)

| Candidate requirement | Evidence required before advancing |
| --- | --- |
| On a working LAN without internet, a first-time authorized teammate can join a selected group and receive a usable document. Sender and recipient can tell whether bytes were saved. | Observe the current flow with internet egress disabled, an excluded nearby account, an offline/reconnecting recipient and a late joiner. Measure time, steps and repeated confusion. Check consent, integrity, audience and recovery after sender exit with and without available authorized file custody. Advance only a reproducible gap. |
| An authorized teammate can exchange a short asynchronous voice message when typing or immediate live conversation is impractical. | Establish demand and compare existing audio-file transfer and calling. Qualify recording permission and cleanup, consent to download/play, visible delivery state, codec support, size and retention caps, and the behavior on interruption and resume. Test cold start and offline playback of received bytes. |
| An authorized pair can hold an intelligible live conversation over the named topology and hardware. | Compare current direct calling first. Require both audible receive paths and measurements of setup time, usable audio under loss, cutoff/reconnect, device release on hangup/lock and permission failure. Approve explicit latency, bandwidth, power and airtime limits before judging a profile. Push-to-talk, full-duplex calls, group voice and live video each need their own demand and acceptance evidence. |
| Nearby authorized peers can exchange short text when no usable IP path exists. | Establish a recurring population, distance, device mix and workload. Reproduce with WAN and infrastructure LAN unavailable, then with a LAN that blocks peer traffic. Test direct and forced multi-hop, partition/merge, install and pairing, lock/sleep, recovery, and idle return on supported native platforms. Measure latency, delivery, power and bounded queues. A BLE trial needs compatible radios and permissions. A LoRa trial additionally needs supported radio hardware, firmware and region-appropriate operating settings and airtime limits. Qualify voice and files separately. |
| An authorized peer can get a usable attachment or shared page in the target network conditions. | Classify the payload as a link, inline/cacheable media, a completed file, or a live stream. With internet cut, test content from authorized local sources and unreachable external URLs. Establish typical sizes, time to usable bytes, explicit expiry and limits, handling of interrupted or unavailable sources, and what the sender can infer. |
| If forwarding or an external transport becomes necessary, it preserves Mesh Talk identity, contact permissions and bounded retention. | Specify who discovers, routes, persists, and acknowledges; who can verify, forward or decrypt; and what metadata is visible. Test unauthorized recipients, stale identities, expired records, duplicates, lost acknowledgments and partition recovery. Verify protocol, licenses, dependency updates, runtime/battery costs and fallback before adopting any binding or new radio. See the existing contract owners for network and resource decisions. |

[Mesh Talk network design](../docs/network-design-reference.md) · [Module ownership](../docs/module-boundaries.md) · [Performance requirements](../docs/performance-requirements.md)

The desk evidence supports testing the LAN handoff scenario against today's baseline. Radio fallback, bridge selection and alternate voice modes remain conditional on observed need and native evidence. The cited projects provide precedents and test cases. They supply neither product rankings nor acceptance measurements for Mesh Talk.

Saved the [REQ-029 research notes](/Users/kingsonwu/programming/OctopusGarage/mesh-talk/.worktrees/req-029/tmp/req-029-mesh-sources.md) with 55 source links and seven candidate requirements, each with an evidence gate.

- **Columba** implements live encrypted voice over LXST and sends photos, files, and recorded voice over LXMF. LoRa requires external RNode hardware. Call quality over a specific radio path remains unverified. [Columba source](https://github.com/torlando-tech/columba) · [Reticulum hardware manual](https://reticulum.network/manual/hardware.html#rnode)
- **Bitchat** supports live push-to-talk, recorded voice notes, and small files over nearby BLE without an infrastructure LAN. Nostr fallback requires internet access. [Apple voice protocol](https://github.com/permissionlesstech/bitchat/blob/v1.8.0/bitchat/Protocols/VoiceBurstPacket.swift#L21) · [Bitchat whitepaper](https://github.com/permissionlesstech/bitchat/blob/main/WHITEPAPER.md)
- **Technitium Mesh** is confirmed as the Windows P2P messenger that supports chat and file transfer over a reachable LAN without internet. **tromoSM/HostTalk** is a plausible match for the original lead. It uses a reachable local web host, and the original reference remains unconfirmed. [Technitium Mesh](https://mesh.im/) · [HostTalk upstream](https://github.com/tromoSM/HostTalk)

This was a source review. Runtime reliability, platform parity, and user demand remain unmeasured. No builds or commits were made.

**English note**  
Original — “identify possible HostTalk source without conflation”  
Better — “Identify a possible source for HostTalk and distinguish it from similarly named products.”  
Why — “Distinguish it from” makes the comparison explicit.  
Useful pattern — “This is a plausible match, but the original reference is still unconfirmed.”
